title: Contributing to copynumber
text: Fork package clone onto computer. haven’t done , recommend using usethis::create_from_github("igordot/copynumber", fork = TRUE). Install development dependencies devtools::install_dev_deps(), make sure package passes R CMD check running devtools::check(). R CMD check doesn’t pass cleanly, ’s good idea ask help continuing. Create Git branch pull request (PR). recommend using usethis::pr_init("brief-description--change"). Make changes, commit git, create PR running usethis::pr_push(), following prompts browser. title PR briefly describe change. body PR contain Fixes #issue-number. user-facing changes, add bullet top NEWS.md (.e. just first header). Follow style described https://style.tidyverse.org/news.html.

text: data input copynumber package normalized log-transformed copy number measurements, one several samples. Allele-frequencies may also specified segmentation SNP-array data. data organized data matrix row represents probe, first two columns give chromosomes genomic positions (locally chromosome) corresponding probe. title: An overview of the copynumber package
text: copynumber package provides three segmentation tools. method pcf handles single-sample case, segmentation done independently sample data set, break points thus differ sample sample. method multipcf runs multiple samples simultaneously, fits segmentation curves common break points samples. segment values sample equal average measurement segment. third method, aspcf, intended SNP array data performs allele-specific segmentation. results segmentation curves break points common LogR BAF data individual samples.

title: An overview of the copynumber package
text: important parameter set segmentation routines gamma, determines penalty applied discontinuity break point segmentation curve. Note default value appropriate data sets; may depend purpose study artifacts may arise experimental procedure. Hence typically necessary test number gamma values find optimal one. valuable tool context diagnostic tool plotGamma, segmentation run 10 different values gamma results displayed multigrid plot. allows user explore appropriateness segmentation result. Another parameter influences segmentation result kmin, imposes minimum length (number probes) segment.

title: An overview of the copynumber package
text: Several tools available package plotting data segmentation results. include plotGenome, plotSample, plotChrom data /segments plotted entire genome, given sample across different chromosomes given chromosome across different samples, respectively. graphical tools include plotHeatmap, plots copy numbers heatmaps, plotFreq, plots frequency samples aberration genomic position. addition, plotCircle enables plotting genome circle aberration frequencies connections genomic loci added middle circle.

title: An overview of the copynumber package
text: package includes three data sets used examples : lymphoma: 3K aCGH data subset 21 samples (Eide et al., 2010). micma: subset 244K aCGH data set. Contains data chromosome 17 6 samples (Mathiesen et al., 2011). logR BAF: Artificial 10K SNP array data 2 samples.

title: An overview of the copynumber package
text: illustrate allele-specific segmentation, apply artificial SNP-array data set containing LogR data BAF data: start Winsorizing LogR data: function aspcf perform allele-specific segmentation, taking (Winsorized) LogR data BAF data input: Note output similar pcf, except extra 8’th column giving segment BAF-values. function plotAllele may used plot data segmentation results. given sample results shown LogR- BAF-track chromosomes different panels, illustrated first sample chromosomes 1-4. Allele-specific plot one sample chromosomes 1-4. Segmentation done aspcf.

title: An overview of the copynumber package
text: useful graphical tool plotFreq, plot frequency samples data set gain loss genomic position. example use pcf obtain copy number estimates entire lymphoma data set: Gains losses regions copy number estimate defined thresholds specified parameters thres.gain thres.loss, respectively. code: lymphoma.res <- pcf(data = lymphoma, gamma = 12, verbose = FALSE) plotFreq(segments = lymphoma.res, thres.gain = 0.2, thres.loss = -0.1)
